chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Mu'awiyah said:

I asked him about the prayer of the two Eids, and he said: 'Two rak'ahs, with nothing before them or after them, and there is no Adhan or Iqamah in them. He says twelve Takbirs in them. He begins by saying Takbir and initiating the prayer, then recites Al-Fatiha, then recites "Wa ash-shamsi wa duha-ha". Then he says five Takbirs, then says Takbir and bows, so he bows with the seventh (Takbir), and prostrates two prostrations. Then he stands up and recites Al-Fatiha and "Hasataka hadith al-ghashiyah". Then he says four Takbirs, prostrates two prostrations, and recites the Tashahhud.'

He said: 'And so did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). The Khutbah is after the prayer, and it was Uthman who introduced the Khutbah before the prayer. And when the Imam delivers the sermon, he should sit for a little between the two sermons. And it is appropriate for the Imam to wear a Burdah (cloak) on the days of the two Eids, whether it is made of wool or hair, and to go out to the open ground where one can see the horizons of the sky, and not to pray on a mat, nor prostrate upon it. And indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to go out to Al-Baqi' and lead the people in prayer.'

key_terms.صَلاَةُ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ: Prayer of the two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)
key_terms.هَلْ أَتاكَ حَدِيثُ اَلْغاشِيَةِ: Has there reached you the news of the Overwhelming (Surah Al-Ghashiyah)
key_terms.وَ اَلشَّمْسِ وَ ضُحاها: And the Sun and its brightness (Surah Ash-Shams)

ai.seo_question: What are the detailed steps and rulings for performing the Eid prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the canonical form of the Eid prayer, emphasizing the twelve Takbirs and the post-prayer sermon, while noting that the pre-prayer sermon was an innovation by Caliph Uthman. It further prescribes specific etiquette for the Imam, such as wearing a turban and praying in an open field, reflecting the Prophet’s practice of gathering the community in spacious areas like Al-Baqi to connect with the broader creation.
